sources.title: Context Rot: How increasing input tokens impacts LLM performance (HN discussion)
sources.summary: HN thread on Chroma's context-rot study; practitioners report coding-agent quality degrading across long sessions and after repeated compactions.
key_facts: 260 points, 59 comments, July 14 2025
posnet: "Claude Code with Opus or Sonnet gets worse the more compactions happen, quality regresses."
milchek: "The longer a conversation goes on in Cursor about a feature, the worse output gets consistently."
boesboes: "Claude loses ability to distinguish between its own mistakes and instructions once confused."
Workaccount2: good instance fumbles for ~20k tokens then session is 'heavily rotted'; needs manual pruning
irskep: "Compactions reduce transcripts to summaries, losing information beyond just context rot effects."
mikeve: long transcripts make models return generic summaries instead of answering

sources.title: Context rot: the emerging challenge that could hold back LLM progress
sources.summary: Explainer on Chroma's context-rot research: performance degrades as input grows across all 18 models tested, well before the advertised window.
key_facts: Term 'context rot' coined June 2025 by an HN commenter, then measured by Chroma
Chroma tested 18 models incl. GPT-4.1, Claude 4 family, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3
Accuracy drops non-uniformly with input length, sometimes 30-50% before documented limit (per search summary)
Positional bias: relevant info buried mid-context is handled worst

sources.title: Sarah Wooders (Letta) on 'context rot' and sleeptime agents
sources.summary: Letta co-founder endorses the term and describes their mitigation: asynchronous 'sleeptime' agents that rewrite context blocks.
key_facts: "'context rot' is a good term and something we've seen a lot with long-running agents"
Letta mitigates by using sleeptime agents to re-write context blocks asynchronously
Positions memory-block rewriting as the vendor answer to long-session degradation

sources.title: Auto-compact triggers mid-task causing context loss and hallucinations (claude-code #10948)
sources.summary: Canonical Claude Code complaint: auto-compaction fires mid-task with no warning, summary drops file edits and decisions, agent derails.
key_facts: Opened Nov 4 2025
"Auto-compact triggers ... no user control, no warning before compaction, and no way to disable or configure."
"Claude loses track of what was actually done vs what needs to be done"
Summary "loses track of file modifications, intermediate decisions, specific technical details, and conflates what was planned vs implemented"
Workarounds: /rewind (loses subsequent work), fresh chat with manual context, or 'elaborate checkpoint/handover workflows'
Requested fixes: disable via settings, better summarization fidelity, prompt before compaction

sources.title: Claude Skills context completely lost after auto-compaction (claude-code #13919)
sources.summary: After auto-compaction Claude Code forgets the Skills it was actively using, causing repeated errors and 'massive productivity loss'.
key_facts: Reporter: skills context 'completely lost after auto-compaction, causing repeated errors and massive productivity loss'
Related #27955: in plan mode, auto-compact loses plan context and executes partial work without creating plan file
Related #13112: 'Auto-Compact causes context loss and degraded performance'

sources.title: CLAUDE.md context lost after /compact - re-inject project instructions (claude-code #24460)
sources.summary: Project-level instructions (CLAUDE.md) drop out of the window after compaction; users ask for automatic re-injection.
key_facts: Request: automatically re-inject CLAUDE.md after /compact
Shows compaction discards not only history but standing instructions
Related #28721: 'Conversation compaction causes context loss and performance degradation'

sources.title: Auto compact does not trigger at 100% context window and Claude Code stops itself (claude-code #66144)
sources.summary: Mid-2026 report: compaction fails to fire, session hits 100% and halts; related issue says auto-compact option disappeared and responses slow as context grows.
key_facts: Reported June 2026 (per search summary)
At limit, 'no automatic compaction happens ... simply reaches 100% context and stops'
Related #37914: 'Auto-compact option missing after recent update - context grows large and responses become very slow'
Related #26858: Claude Code freezes before auto-compaction triggers inside Cursor (Sonnet 4.6)

sources.title: Aggressive context compaction with opus-4.6:1m (cline #9181)
sources.summary: Cline auto-compacts under 200K even on a 1M-context model; users report the agent 'gets a little lost' after compaction during execution.
key_facts: Compaction began when context reached under 200K despite opus-4.6:1m
"Cline gets a little lost afterwards"
Users see context bar run backwards; Cline then 'tries to redo already-completed tasks or forgets important information'

sources.title: Cline auto compacts context silently even with autocompacting setting disabled (cline #10637)
sources.summary: Cline compacts without consent; companion issue #13127 shows local-model summaries truncated at 1024 tokens so compaction silently skips.
key_facts: Auto-compaction runs even with the setting disabled
#13127: summaries for long contexts cut at 1024 tokens -> parse failure -> 'Compaction skipped'
Pattern: compaction is opaque and uncontrollable across tools

sources.title: Cursor's compression isn't a bug. It's how it works.
sources.summary: Argues Cursor's prompt-based summarization structurally changes the context the model was reasoning in, so degradation after compaction is by design.
key_facts: Cursor compression = prompt-based summarization
Post-compaction context is 'structurally different from the one the model was reasoning in earlier'
Practitioner framing: after compaction the model is 'like waking up after sleep with memory loss' (per search summary)

sources.title: Delete partial.json before compaction to avoid losing the summary (coder/mux PR #1007)
sources.summary: A harness-level race condition where the compaction summary itself could be lost from context due to stale partial files.
key_facts: Compaction summary could be dropped from context because of stale partial.json
Fix: delete partial.json before compaction
Shows compaction plumbing is fragile even in third-party harnesses

sources.title: Memory Injection Attacks on LLM Agents via Query-Only Interaction (MINJA)
sources.summary: Shows an attacker can poison an agent's long-term memory using only ordinary queries, no write access, with very high success.
key_facts: MINJA achieves over 95% injection success rate
Works via 'bridging steps', an 'indication prompt', and 'progressive shortening'
Attacker needs no elevated access: any regular user can poison memory
NeurIPS 2025 poster (Sept 18 2025)
Poisoned memory survives session restarts, context resets and model updates

sources.title: Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense on Memory Based LLM-Agents
sources.summary: 2026 follow-up formalising attacks and defenses on memory-based agents; part of a growing defense literature.
key_facts: Defense papers cluster in 2026: SMSR (arXiv 2606.12703, 'certified defence'), MEMSAD (2605.03482), MemAudit (2605.23723), forensic trajectory signatures (2606.30566)
Signals that memory security is now a recognised sub-field, not a one-off

sources.title: AI Memory Security: Best Practices and Implementation
sources.summary: Vendor guidance on securing memory stores against injection and data leakage; shows incumbents responding to poisoning/privacy concern.
key_facts: Frames memory poisoning as persistent: survives context resets
Vendor acknowledgement that memory security is a buying concern

sources.title: Context engineering for AI agents in 2026 (LangChain State of Agent Engineering findings)
sources.venue_or_author: Reactify Solutions summarising LangChain 2026 State of Agent Engineering
sources.summary: Summarises LangChain's 2026 survey: large enterprises name context engineering at scale as the top agent challenge.
key_facts: LangChain 2026 State of Agent Engineering surveyed 1,300+ professionals
57% of organisations run agents in production, another 30% building toward it
Enterprises with 10,000+ employees cited 'context engineering and managing context at scale' as the top challenge
"Quality, not capability, is the bottleneck - and quality at agent scale is a context problem."
Official langchain.com report URL not retrieved (search budget); LinkedIn recap: linkedin.com/posts/coltonbaker88_state-of-ai-agents-activity-7429646732030005249-7ybE

sources.title: The State of AI Agent Memory in 2026: What the Research Actually Shows
sources.summary: Practitioner round-up of memory research; stresses the remember/forget decision and absent enterprise governance.
key_facts: Agents accumulate so much 'important' info that searching memory becomes slower than processing full context
Frameworks lack enterprise governance features like glossary, lineage, entity resolution
Framework fragmentation: 13 agent-framework integrations cited as symptom

sources.title: AI Agent Memory 2026: Progress Benchmark Report Evaluations
sources.summary: Mem0's own 2026 state-of-memory report; vendor framing of benchmark progress.
key_facts: Vendor-authored benchmark report; treat scores as marketing until independently reproduced
Mem0 cloud memory criticised elsewhere as lock-in: no portability, no cryptographic integrity (per O'Reilly/Medium coverage)

sources.title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus
sources.summary: Foundational production post: cache hit rate is the key metric, tool-list churn invalidates cache, and irreversible compression is dangerous.
key_facts: Published July 18 2025; framework rebuilt 4 times ('Stochastic Graduate Descent')
Average input:output token ratio ~100:1; ~50 tool calls per task
Claude Sonnet cached $0.30/MTok vs uncached $3/MTok - 10x
"Even a single-token difference can invalidate the cache from that token onward."
Mask tools, don't remove: adding/removing tools invalidates KV-cache
"You can't reliably predict which observation might become critical ten steps later." -> use file system as context, keep compression restorable
Keep the wrong stuff in: "Without evidence, the model can't adapt."
Few-shot rut: "The model will tend to follow that pattern, even when it's no longer optimal."

sources.title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
sources.summary: Argues parallel subagents fail because they lack shared context and traces; proposes dedicated compression models for long tasks.
key_facts: Published June 12 2025
Principle 1: share context and full agent traces, not just individual messages
Principle 2: actions carry implicit decisions; conflicting decisions produce poor results
Flappy Bird example: one subagent builds a Super Mario background, the other an incompatible bird
"Context engineering is the next level of this. It is about doing this automatically in a dynamic system."
For tasks exceeding the window, compress history with a specialised model - 'demands significant domain-specific refinement'

sources.title: How and when to build multi-agent systems
sources.summary: LangChain's response to Cognition: multi-agent works when context engineering is done deliberately; otherwise handoffs lose decisions.
key_facts: Positions context engineering as the #1 job of agent builders
Counterpoint to 'don't build multi-agents': the failure is context sharing, not parallelism per se

sources.title: What we found after auditing 10,134 mem0 entries: 97.8% were junk (mem0 #4573)
sources.summary: A user audit of a production Mem0 store found almost all entries were noise; extraction prompt, not the model, was the bottleneck.
key_facts: Opened March 27 2026; 10,134 entries audited, 97.8% junk
Only 38 entries usable as-is, 186 after rewriting
Junk: boot-file/system-prompt restating ~3,200 (52.7%), heartbeat noise ~700, architecture dumps ~500, transient task state ~450, hallucinated user profiles ~315
"The extraction prompt is the bottleneck, not the model."
"Any hallucination that gets stored once will be re-extracted indefinitely."
"Indiscriminate memory storage performs worse than using no memory at all."
"The prompt teaches what to extract but never what to skip."

sources.title: ADD-only extraction in v3 may surface stale/contradictory facts for time-sensitive attributes (mem0 #4956)
sources.summary: Mutable attributes (employer, city, relationship) accumulate contradictions and stale facts rank first because scoring ignores recency.
key_facts: Contradictory memories accumulate instead of newer fact superseding older
Retrieval can return outdated info as top candidate because scoring lacks recency
Related #5867 (ADD-only creates conflicting memories), #4896 (no conflict resolution), #4536, discussion #4787 (dedup/contradiction at scale)

sources.title: hash-dedup TOCTOU race in add() creates duplicate memories under concurrency (mem0 #6531)
sources.summary: Concurrent add() calls both pass the dedup check and write identical memories with different IDs.
key_facts: V3 pipeline snapshots memories early, checks dedup after LLM round-trip -> TOCTOU race
Related #5330: no built-in expiration or decay; stale entries pollute context

sources.title: Feature: evaluation toolkit for agent memory quality and retrieval reliability (mem0 #5235)
sources.summary: Users ask for a memory-specific eval module because RAG metrics miss forgetting, update propagation, temporal relevance and conflicts.
key_facts: Opened May 22 2026
"memory is one of the most common sources of subtle, hard-to-reproduce failures"
"the agent should remember a preference but silently retrieves stale or conflicting information instead"
"Regressions in memory behavior go undetected until they affect user experience"
"There's no way to benchmark different embedding models or retrieval strategies for memory use cases"
Proposed metrics: recall rate, staleness score, conflict-resolution accuracy, update-propagation rate

sources.title: Lies, Damn Lies, Statistics: Is Mem0 Really SOTA in Agent Memory?
sources.summary: Zep rebuts Mem0's benchmark claims and argues LoCoMo cannot discriminate memory systems since full-context beats them.
key_facts: Published May 6 2025 (modified June 3 2026)
Zep correct implementation 75.14% vs Mem0 Graph ~68% vs full-context baseline ~73% on LoCoMo
Mem0's paper reported Zep at 65.99% due to setup errors (single-user model, timestamps appended to messages, sequential searches)
LoCoMo conversations only 16k-26k tokens; fails to test knowledge updates; has missing ground truths
"If simply providing all the text yields better results than the specialized memory system, the benchmark isn't adequately stressing memory capabilities."
Calls for LongMemEval-style benchmarks (avg 115k tokens)

sources.title: agentic-memory benchmarks (lhl)
sources.summary: Independent benchmark showing a plain filesystem+grep agent beats a specialised memory system on LoCoMo.
key_facts: Filesystem agent using grep/search_files on gpt-4o-mini scored 74.0% on LoCoMo, above Mem0
Suggests tool-use capability matters more than the retrieval mechanism underneath
LoCoMo scores above ~93% described as suspect; 'directional signal' only

sources.title: Locomo-Plus: Beyond-Factual Cognitive Memory Evaluation Framework for LLM Agents
sources.summary: New benchmark arguing string-match metrics and explicit task prompting misrepresent real memory use; tests cue-trigger semantic disconnect.
key_facts: Conventional string-matching metrics 'misaligned with realistic scenarios'
Companion 2026 work: AMA-Bench (2602.22769) for long-horizon agent memory; A-TMA (2607.01935) on state-aware memory failures
Critique (per search summary): LoCoMo assumes stationary user intent, ignores stale preference reuse, incorrect overwrites, unsafe retention

sources.title: Actually, MCP wastes a lot of tokens when compared to regular tool calling (HN)
sources.summary: HN thread where practitioners quantify how tool schemas and intermediate results flood the window and propose code-execution instead.
key_facts: Parent submission: 'What if you don't need MCP at all?'
rcarmo: MCP 'wastes a lot of tokens ... for locked down/local/cheap models it makes very little sense'
cstrahan: tool descriptions can mean 'hundreds of thousands of tokens before reading a request'
cstrahan: every intermediate result passes through the model; transcript 'flows through twice ... could mean 50,000 tokens'
Alternative: code reads a 50,000-token file and returns 20 tokens to the LLM
didibus: protocol has no mechanism to pipe one tool's output into another

sources.title: MCP Tool Schema Bloat: The Hidden Token Tax (and How to Fix It)
sources.summary: Measures how much of the window MCP schemas consume before any user input.
key_facts: 7 MCP servers = 67,300 tokens of tool definitions = 33.7% of a 200k window
GitHub official MCP server = 17,600 tokens per request
StackOne: MCP definitions can burn 55,000+ tokens before first user message; distinguishes schema bloat vs response bloat (stackone.com/blog/mcp-token-optimization)

sources.title: Code execution with MCP: building more efficient AI agents
sources.summary: Anthropic's incumbent response to tool bloat: load tools on demand and run them as code so intermediate results stay out of context.
key_facts: Three interventions Nov 2025-Feb 2026: Anthropic Tool Search Tool, Cloudflare Code Mode, MCP code-execution pattern
Shared idea: stop loading tool definitions you aren't using
HN 'MCP is dead?' debate: 195 points, 174 comments (per The Agent Report, May 2026)

sources.title: Production RAG: Why Retrieval Fails and How to Fix It
sources.summary: Practitioner guide: most RAG failures are retrieval failures; hybrid + reranker is the floor.
key_facts: Naive RAG (fixed chunks + single-vector) fails to retrieve correct context ~40% of the time
Identifier blindness: dense-only retrieval misses exact-match clause IDs
Right chunk at rank 4, generator latches onto rank 1 -> missing reranker
A ~50 ms rerank step lifts answer quality 10-25% on production traffic
Hybrid + contextual techniques cut error ~69% vs naive vector-only

sources.title: Why RAG Systems Fail in Production
sources.summary: Silent failures are the defining trait of production RAG: confident answers, no error signal, discovered weeks later.
key_facts: "The system answers confidently. No error signal is returned." Users discover bad answers weeks or months later
Chunking at 512 tokens breaks paragraphs and separates questions from answers
Embedding similarity != relevance; top-K is crude
Stanford Law 2025 evaluation: legal RAG tools hallucinated 17-33% on 200 queries (per Atlan summary)

sources.title: Six Lessons Learned Building RAG Systems in Production
sources.summary: Lessons-from-production post on RAG; complements the failure-mode guides with evaluation and chunking advice.
key_facts: 2025 clinical study: adaptive chunking 87% retrieval accuracy vs 13% fixed-size on same dataset (per search summary)
Industry surveys cited: 70-85% of agents fail in production; AI project failures up 42% 2024->2025 (per search summary)

sources.title: Whoever Owns the Memory Owns the Agent
sources.summary: Aug 2026 essay arguing hosted memory is the new lock-in point and memory should be user-owned and portable.
key_facts: Mem0 cloud memory: stored in vendor infra, 'no cryptographic verification of memory integrity', no portability to other systems
Vendor SDKs 'remove orchestration friction and lock the agent to one provider's API'

sources.title: Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Provenance-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous LLM Agents
sources.summary: Proposes an open protocol to serialise, transport and re-hydrate agent memory across systems with cryptographic integrity.
key_facts: Aims at cross-vendor memory transfer with provenance verification
Parallel effort: MemoryLake 'memory passport for agents' (platform-neutral, user-owned layer)
Cognee (Apache 2.0, 14,000+ GitHub stars) cited as reference open-source memory without lock-in (per XLR8 roundup)

sources.title: The AI Agents Stack (2026 Edition)
sources.summary: Analyst view: memory is now a first-class architectural layer outside the prompt, with three tiers; lock-in of vendor SDKs flagged.
key_facts: Production agents in 2026 keep memory in a dedicated layer outside the prompt
Memory described as 'first-class architectural primitive with three distinct tiers'
Companion: O'Reilly 'Open Source Agent Toolkit in 2026' lists per-layer OSS alternatives

sources.title: Context rot explained (& how to prevent it)
sources.summary: Infrastructure incumbent (Redis) publishing context-rot guidance, signalling the problem has mainstream vendor attention.
key_facts: Agents accumulate noise during search, exploration and backtracking that degrades every subsequent output
Incumbent databases positioning as the fix for context rot
